title: LLM Serving Optimization with Variable Prefill and Decode Lengths: an unbounded approximation ratio for the benchmark policy (Theorem 1)
author: Meixuan Wang, Yinyu Ye, Zijie Zhou
work: LLM Serving Optimization with Variable Prefill and Decode Lengths
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the theorem printed as Theorem 1 of "LLM Serving Optimization with Variable Prefill and Decode Lengths" (source0.tex lines 223--230, source label thm:benchmark), delivered with the article's own complete proof at source0.tex lines 853--897 (45 lines, the article's own appendix proof environment whose header names the theorem). The theorem is the article's negative main result: it exhibits a family of finite feasible instances of the KV-cache batch scheduling problem, indexed by an unbounded sequence of capacities M, on which the natural shortest-decode-first benchmark policy MC-SF has an approximation ratio tending to infinity. The proof is complete inside the retained span: it constructs m^4 type-A requests with (s_i,o_i)=(3m^2-1,1) and m^5 type-B requests with (s_i,o_i)=(1,2) at capacity M=3m^4, verifies individual feasibility, shows that MC-SF serves all type-A requests first, computes the forced start boundaries and the resulting total end-to-end latency lower bound of order m^5 m^2, compares it with the optimal latency of order m^4, and concludes that the ratio grows at least like m/8 while the requests stay well inside the capacity. It is above ordinary PhD qualifying level: the argument requires modelling the memory footprint of prefill and decode tokens, the head-of-line admission rule and the resulting schedule boundaries of a non-trivial online scheduling problem, and it establishes an unbounded approximation ratio for a policy proposed in the recent literature. Rated H2 because it is a self-contained adversarial construction with a short accounting rather than a long multi-lemma proof chain.
